prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Edit target: the attached saloon and Poncho mockup. Keep EXACTLY its composition, object positions, orthogonal overhead camera, character identity, colors and silhouettes. Make only ONE CHANGE: replace ALL smooth shading and softly textured rendering with strict limited-palette low-resolution pixel-art construction.

The previous result is still TOO SOFT and shaded like a small digital painting. Redraw every surface with large perfectly uniform flat color clusters and brutally crisp hard edges. NO smooth gradients on blue floor, cream wall, hat, wood, chair seats, barrel or pot. NO antialiasing, blended edge colors, colored fringe pixels, translucent shadows, texture noise, bilinear scaling, diagonal lines thinner than the native grid. Give each material only THREE SOLID COLORS: shadow, base, highlight, with clear geometric boundaries. The floor uses only two quiet blue-gray flat colors, one for uniform tile faces and another for simple grout. Cream wall one flat cream fill. Shadow uses a single uniform dark desaturated tone. Character highest contrast. Preserve broad warm golden sombrero, raised olive crown, brown triangular fabric reaching ground and covering feet, revolver to right. Make his fringe fewer and bolder chunky stepped shapes, not fine lines.

Think an actual hand-placed 240 by 180 pixel tile-based game screenshot enlarged exactly SIX times with nearest-neighbor. Output landscape 4:3. Every visible native pixel is one solid square; all diagonal outlines are staircases of identical square grid units; no new detail smaller than that unit. Crisp clean early 1990s SNES sprite craftsmanship, NOT a simulated mosaic filter, not blurry retro emulation. Keep the bar, two chairs, card table, bottle shelf, clay pot, barrel and rug. No additional objects, no text, no HUD, no frame.
